summary: MoreOOP is a Java-based combat simulation project inspired by Lord of the Rings characters. It is designed as a laboratory assignment for a university object-oriented programming course to demonstrate inheritance, polymorphism, and dynamic class loading using the Reflections library.
strengths: Good use of object-oriented programming principles, specifically inheritance with the Character base class and polymorphism with overridden kick methods.
Dynamic character instantiation in CharacterFactory using the Reflections library, allowing new character types to be integrated seamlessly without modifying the factory class.
Automated unit testing with JUnit 5 and basic test coverage for character behaviors.
Automated CI workflow defined in GitHub Actions to compile code and run tests on push.
issues: Potential infinite loop in GameManager: if two Hobbits fight, they will loop indefinitely crying without dealing any damage to each other.
Poor encapsulation: the power and hp fields in the Character base class are public, exposing class internals and bypassing getters and setters.
Character class could be abstract: the base Character class has an empty kick implementation and can be instantiated directly, which should be avoided.
Reflections library overhead: scanning the classpath at runtime to locate subclasses of Character is slow and introduces a heavy third-party dependency for a small number of static character types.
Lack of input validation: while setHp prevents negative HP, there is no validation on setPower to prevent negative values.
recommendations: Declare the Character class as abstract and make the kick(Character c) method an abstract method.
Change the visibility of power and hp fields to private or protected and enforce encapsulation.
Add a maximum turn limit or a state progress check in GameManager.fight to prevent infinite loop scenarios (e.g. Hobbit vs Hobbit).
Replace runtime classpath scanning in CharacterFactory with a static registration list or a lightweight factory pattern to eliminate the third-party reflections dependency.
Improve unit test coverage by adding tests for King, Knight, CharacterFactory, and GameManager.
